summary: Napa County lookout on Berryessa Peak, built 1948 (CDF 809R design), destroyed by the Rumsey Fire in October 2004; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: CDF 809R design, 30-foot K-brace enclosed steel tower
facts.status_note: Destroyed by the Rumsey Fire in October 2004; register lists it as removed in 2004
facts.agency: Disputed: U.S. Forest Service per the Former Fire Lookout Sites register; California Department of Forestry (CAL FIRE) per West Lookouts and Wikipedia

corrections.why: The register describes a 30 foot K-Brace enclosed steel tower (about 9.1 m); 17.4 m (about 57 ft) is not supported by any source read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says Administered by U.S. Forest Service and places it in Mendocino National Forest; West Lookouts files it under the California Department of Forestry and Wikipedia calls it a CAL FIRE tower. Both are reported in the story and neither is chosen.

sources.title: Forest Fire Lookout Association, Western Region report, 2004
Berryessa Peak Lookout dedication, Napa, 1948
sources.publisher: Internet Archive (California Division of Forestry Black Cards collection, Cal Fire Museum)

notes_for_editor: Brief height_m 17.4 conflicts with the register's 30 ft tower; corrected to 9.1. Agency is disputed across sources (USFS per register; CDF/CAL FIRE per West Lookouts and Wikipedia) and the story says so. The Rumsey Fire citation is Wikipedia, used as a lead; its dates and arson finding are from its own text, which cites CAL FIRE reports that were not read. A Record Net 2004 article was blocked (HTTP 403). The Internet Archive record is public domain; no image URL was retrieved, so no photos entry. No staffing information found. Nothing read describes the site today. A non-primary summary says the tower was built in 1949; not used, the register and the 1948 photo record agree on 1948.
